node.title: Re: ternary conditional help
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [opaltoot],

[tybalt89] already gave you [id://1176732|the answer], I just wanted to note you can use [doc://B::Deparse] to see how Perl interprets your code for yourself (I replaced 1 with $x to prevent optimization):

$ perl -MO=Deparse,-p -e '$x ? $a = 2 : $b = "x";' (($x ? ($a = 2) : $b) = 'x'); $ perl -MO=Deparse,-p -e '$x ? ($a = 2) : ($b = "x");' ($x ? ($a = 2) : ($b = 'x'));

See also [doc://perlop#Operator-Precedence-and-Associativity].

Although you might want to consider if using the ternary operator like that will help the legibility of the code :-)

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
